'''Sorkhei''' is a [[Western Iranian language|Northwestern Iranian language]]. It is one of the Komisenian languages.<ref>{{Glottolog|komi1276|Komisenian}}</ref> It is spoken in the village of [[Sorkheh]] in [[Semnan province]] in northwestern Iran.<ref>Lecoq, pg. 297</ref>

== Classification ==
Sorkhei is a Northwestern Iranian language and belongs to the Komisenian subgroup''.'' It is linguistically close to Sangsari, Lasgerdi and Aftari.<ref>{{Glottolog|komi1276|Komisenian}}</ref> Sorkhei also shares similar structures with [[Zaza language|Zaza]], which is linguistically close to [[Semnani language|Semnani]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last=Paul |first=Ludwig |date=1998 |title=The Pozition of Zazaki the West Iranian Languages |url=https://www.iranchamber.com/literature/articles/zazaki_among_iranian_languages.pdf |access-date=October 28, 2025 |website=Iran Chamber |publisher=Open Publishing}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Gippert |first=Jost |date=2008 |title=Zur dialektalen Stellung des Zazaki |journal=Die Sprache |volume=47 |issue=1 |pages=103|author-link=Jost Gippert}}</ref>

== History ==
During the [[Iran-Iraq War]], radio operators from [[Sorkheh]] used the language as a form of [[secure voice|cryptography]] for [[tactical communications]] of the [[Islamic Republic of Iran Armed Forces|Iranian Armed Forces]].<ref>[https://www.mehrnews.com/news/2876629/%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D8%AE%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AF%D9%86%DB%8C-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%B2%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%B3%D8%B1%DB%8C-%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%AE%D9%87 Mehr (in Persian)]</ref>

During the [[Iran nuclear negotiations]], the language was used in conversations between Iranian President [[Hassan Rouhani]] and [[Hossein Fereydoun]], his brother and [[Aide to the President of Iran|aide]] traveling with the negotiating team. This was done to eliminate or reduce comprehensibility of the conversation by any potential [[eavesdrop]]pers.<ref>[http://www.tabnak.ir/fa/news/521419/%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%AA-%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%82%DA%86%DB%8C-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%DA%AF%D9%81%D8%AA-%D9%88-%DA%AF%D9%88%DB%8C-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%AD%D8%A7%D9%86%DB%8C-%D8%A8%D9%87-%DA%AF%D9%88%DB%8C%D8%B4-%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%AE%D9%87-%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D9%85%D8%AB%D9%84%D8%AB-%D8%AC%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D9%85%D8%AC%D9%84%D8%B3-%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%B1%DA%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AA%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%AF-%DA%A9%DB%8C%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%AA%D8%B9%D8%B7%DB%8C%D9%84%DB%8C-%D9%85%D8%AC%D9%84%D8%B3-%D8%A8%D8%AF%D9%87%DA%A9%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D9%85%DB%8C%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AF%DB%8C-%D8%B7%D9%84%D8%A8%DA%A9%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B4%D8%AF Tabnak (in Persian)]</ref>
